children: Australian stocks look set to follow the Dow Jones Industrial Average higher in early trade, continuing their recent recovery. ASX futures are up by 0.1% ahead of Tuesday's session, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 will build on a 1.4% rise compiled over the past two sessions. The benchmark index has bounced almost 2% since Oct. 1, when it hit its lowest close since early June. Ahead of the open, telecommunications provider Telstra maintained its annual guidance. In the U.S., the DJIA rose 0.4% as continued attacks in Ukraine and the Middle East pushed energy stocks and oil prices higher. The S&P 500 slipped less than 0.1% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.4%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
